notes.title: The Art of Control and the Gift of Randomness: How World of Tanks and The Zodiac
notes.notes: [p]If we were to assign zodiac signs to game designers, then the designers of World of Tanks would definitely be precise Virgos, while The Zodiac Mystery designers would be free-spirited Sagittarians.[/p][p]One side tries to deconstruct perfect balance with mathematical formulas, even fine-tuning the armor penetration of a shell. The other tears up the neatly written script, allowing fate to decide which page of the story players will read today.[/p][p]It’s a fascinating philosophical juxtaposition in the world of games. The engineers of World of Tanks resemble meticulous surgeons, performing “operations” to balance gameplay year after year, striving to build a fair competitive universe. The team behindThe Zodiac Mystery, however, steps back from the role of absolute creator, introducing a random system that allows every player to experience a detective story uniquely their own.[/p][p]One eliminates variables, the other creates them. One pursues the optimal solution, the other embraces infinite solutions. Although these design philosophies appear to move in opposite directions, they both ultimately achieve the same goal: to ensure that players feel their choices carry meaning, and that every playthrough is filled with discovery and surprise.[/p][p]Maybe this is where the charm of game design lies. The road to excellence is never singular, and the best designs are often those that understand most deeply what their players truly need.[/p][p] [/p][p][b]World of Tanks: Fairness and Vitality Through Precise Control[/b][/p][p]The designers of World of Tanks act as engineers and referees simultaneously. Their work rests on immense volumes of data, with endless adjustments and iterations. The goal of this work is not to reach an absolutely balanced mathematical model, but to maintain two vital aspects of player experience.[/p][p][b]A Sense of Fairness:[/b] In competitive games, players devote huge amounts of time and effort to honing skills and developing strategies. Their main demand is that victory or defeat hinges on these, rather than the raw numbers of the vehicles they select. Balancing, which nerfs overly strong weapons and strengthens underused ones, exists to safeguard the purity of the game, ensuring that skill and strategy determine outcomes. This sense of fairness is the very cornerstone of PvP gaming.[/p][p][b]A Sense of Vitality:[/b] Any static game system will eventually be “solved” by its community, leading to repeatable optimal strategies. This, in turn, inevitably causes gameplay stagnation and aesthetic fatigue. Regular adjustments act as an external force to disrupt this equilibrium, overturn existing patterns, and push players out of their comfort zones. This compels them to learn, explore, and adapt, contributing novel strategic depth to the game.[/p][p]In this sense, World of Tanks’ philosophy is to shape experience through ultimate control. It’s like a gardener tending to an ecosystem with great care, pruning, fertilizing, and introducing new species in order to sustain its diversity and vitality.[/p][p] [/p][p][b]The Zodiac Mystery: Immersion and Belonging in the Unknown[/b][/p][p]The Zodiac Mystery designers have taken a radically different path, similar to building a stage and then inviting “the unknown” to act as co-director. Rather than controlling every step of the narrative, we allow the triggering of key clues and the appearance of vital evidence to be decided by an independent, random system. This is not laziness, but a deliberate act of empowerment, designed to evoke two profound experiences.[/p][p][b]Immersion:[/b] Real detective work is filled with chance and uncertainty. When players cannot predict whether their next investigation will uncover the truth or lead them deeper into confusion, they abandon the mindset of following a walkthrough and instead rely on their own observation and reasoning. The tension, surprise, and frustration born from this unpredictability create a true sense of immersion.[/p][p][b]Belonging:[/b] Because the random system ensures that no two playthroughs are the same, players encounter unique combinations of clues and may arrive at strikingly different interpretations of the truth. Motivations, even the core of the story itself, may diverge from one playthrough to the next. By surrendering absolute control of the “one truth,” the designers grant players partial ownership of the narrative, creating a powerful sense of personal belonging.[/p][p]The philosophy behind The Zodiac Mystery is one of shaping experience through controlled disorder. It is like scattering seeds and then allowing nature’s rain and sunlight to decide how they grow, trusting that life will find its own unique form. In the end, what emerges is a garden that is unexpected, unrepeatable, and uniquely beautiful.[/p][p] [/p][p][b]Converging Paths: A Shared Commitment to Player Experience[/b][/p][p]On the surface, the “control” of World of Tanks and the “unknown” of The Zodiac Mystery appear as parallel lines that will never meet. Yet in essence, they both address the same fundamental challenge: how to resist monotony in player experience, while maximizing the sense of agency players feel within the game.[/p][p]World of Tanks controls its environment to ensure that player skill can be exercised fairly. The Zodiac Mystery frees its narrative flow so player reasoning remains at the heart of the experience. Each approach precisely addresses the deepest emotional needs of our respective audiences; competitive players seek self-affirmation through fair competition, while narrative players long for self-discovery through immersive worlds.[/p][p]Great game design is never a binary choice between control and chaos. It is the art of knowing when to hold the reins and when to let go. And the single, highest standard of judgment will always remain the same: the quality of the experience it creates for players.[/p]

notes.title: The Algorithm Trust Crisis: The Zodiac Mystery and the Ethics of Randomness
notes.notes: [p]When [i]Honor of Kings[/i] players discovered that their five-kill streaks may have been nothing more than “reward matches” carefully manipulated and staged by the algorithm, and when professional players found themselves trapped in diamond rank, losing 25 out of 33 games under the so-called “system penalty,” a wave of mistrust swept through the gaming industry.[/p][p][i]“We aren’t playing the game—the game is playing us!”“This isn’t about losing streaks, it’s about the betrayal of being treated like disposable batteries…”[/i][/p][p]What players rage against is not the wins and losses themselves, but the despair of being reduced to data, fenced in by algorithms. Once the ELO system transforms from a tool for fair matchmaking into a mechanism for user retention, once victories are degraded from the result of competition into a product of data manipulation, the very essence of gaming has already been distorted. At the heart of this issue lies a fundamental question: should algorithms serve the player, or should players be sacrificed to feed the algorithm?[/p][p][i]The Zodiac Mystery[/i] responds to this crisis with the most rebellious answer of all: if algorithms are destined to become tools of control, then it’s better to surrender that control to the unknown.[/p][p]In the world of [i]The Zodiac Mystery[/i], developers step back from the throne of creation. Their only role is to plant seeds of the story in the soil of the game world. However, the decision of which seed sprouts, when it flowers, and what fruit it bears is left entirely to the “divine rain” cast down by the “Dice of God”—the system’s randomly delivered clues and unexpected events.[/p][p]This is not a superficial technical gimmick, but rather a surgical intervention into a deep-rooted illness of the industry.[/p][p]In an era where algorithms constantly discipline and constrain us, the “Dice of God” delivers not only random clues, but also a long-overdue respect; respect for each and every player, and respect for every possible shape the story might take. What [i]The Zodiac Mystery[/i] rebuilds is not only the emotional value of play, but also a kind of ethics in games that has been steadily eroded.[/p][p]The soul of gaming does not lie in perfectly calculated “balance,” but in the curiosity and awe players feel when confronted with infinite possibilities.[/p]

notes.title: Dice, Puzzles, and Truth: How The Zodiac Mystery Reimagines Multi-Ending Narrati
notes.notes: [p]Imagine a game world where the designer, like a creator, has shaped every detail of light and shadow, given flesh and soul to each character, and buried countless seeds of story—clues, foreshadowing, diverging fates—deep in its soil. Even the bricks on the wall, the paintings in the corridor, or a drifting leaf might conceal a truth that overturns everything.[/p][p]But this time, when the foundations were laid, the [i]The Zodiac Mystery[/i]’s creator took an unprecedented step, withdrawing and leaving a “scepter” glowing with chaotic light suspended in the void.[/p][p]This scepter is not an object, but an independent and uncontrollable system made up of random rules. Once activated, the scepter ceased to be a tool, becoming instead a “god” within the game, able to decide when crucial events occur, when key clues emerge, or even how a character’s fate unfolds. The creator laid the soil and planted the seeds, but which one sprouts, when it flowers, and what fruit it bears depends on the unpredictable “rainfall” of this god. Even the creator cannot foresee the player’s exact path.[/p][p]Multi-ending games are usually designed to escape the monotony of linear storytelling. Designers create branching plots and let player choices at key moments drive the experience, each small variable rippling outward like a stone thrown into water until it produces a different ending.[/p][p]But in reality, many games that promise a “butterfly effect” quietly betray that ideal. Players appear to choose, but in fact they are simply selecting from the developer’s answer bank. This illusion of freedom undermines the experience: instead of feeling the weight of choice, players become task executors, following guides and uncovering preordained results.[/p][p][i]The Zodiac Mystery[/i] breaks from this pattern. By shifting the dynamic from “creator vs. player” to a three-way contest between this “god,” the creator, and the player, it builds not a fixed maze of storylines but a living system of rules and possibilities.[/p][p]Here, the player is no longer a puppet walking a predetermined track, but is actually granted true freedom to observe, think, and adapt. There are no standard answers, no guides to follow. Instead, the player finds themselves in a detective case that evolves dynamically, piecing together truth from the “rainfall” of this god as random clues or unexpected events combine with investigation and character interaction.[/p][p]Every piece of narrative foreshadowing is also subject to this system. A sudden “rainfall” may cause a hidden clue to surface and plunge the player into unforeseen depths, or it may bury another clue in obscurity, leaving it forever unsolved. This interplay between randomness and player reasoning makes every investigation unique and unrepeatable, forcing the player into the detective’s most essential state: facing chaos, embracing uncertainty, and searching for breakthroughs in the clash of chance and logic.[/p][p]In most multiple ending games, players often pursue completion, endlessly repeating processes to unlock every ending. But in [i]The Zodiac Mystery[/i], no single player can, or needs to, see the entire picture. Endings are scattered puzzle pieces, and which ones you pick up depends on the “god’s” random gifts. The aim is not exhaustive collection but to focus on the uniqueness of each journey and let go of anxiety over what remains unseen.[/p][p]When you finish the game, the ending you see is only one possibility born of random rules and your choices together. It is not the creator’s ordained truth. Different players, blessed with different rainfall and encountering different clues, will naturally interpret motives, truths, and characters in different ways. Some may see “A” as a hero of justice, others condemn “B” as a hidden villain, while still others read tragedy in the scattered words of “C.”[/p][p]This is the true vitality of narrative. If all players arrive at the same conclusion, it means the creator’s will has been imposed, and the game has collapsed into a polished piece of indoctrination. By introducing this “god” as a random variable, [i]The Zodiac Mystery[/i] dismantles the creator’s absolute control and returns interpretive power to the players themselves. Their diverse perspectives and contrasting views of human nature create echoes that linger long after play ends.[/p][p]The creator also undergoes a transformation in this three-way dynamic. They are no longer an omniscient puppet master, but the foundation of a world of possibilities. They provide the fertile soil and varied seeds, invite “god” to bring sun and rain, and entrust the harvest to the player’s steps and insight. On this land nourished by both randomness and design, players forge their own path and reap their own unique fruit.[/p][p]Only when the creator releases the strings and lets this “god” cast the decisive dice do players truly gain the right to explore freely, think independently, and define their own endings. In this way, the multi-ending game escapes its designed cage and becomes a living universe of stories, constantly growing and full of life.[/p]

notes.title: Devlog #3: Designing Experience and Emotion in The Zodiac Mystery
notes.notes: [p]When we talk about a game having a “great experience,” we often mean the fusion of two things—the immersive satisfaction of solving a mystery, when scattered clues fall into place like a puzzle and the story’s logic snaps together in your mind, and the emotional resonance of the story, where moments of regret, loyalty, or difficult choices make you feel the weight behind each twist.[/p][p][i]The Zodiac Mystery[/i] isn’t just a game. It’s an immersive, first-person journey into the heart of a case, one that leads you through starlit guidance and foggy dilemmas, where pain and thought, emotion and justice, constantly collide.[/p][p] [/p][p][b]Story: A Carefully Woven Web[/b][/p][p]The story of [i]The Zodiac Mystery[/i] unfolds like a web. It begins with a string of ritualistic murders tied to zodiac signs, instantly pulling you into its layered mystery and urging you to follow the trail.[/p][p]As the investigation deepens, once-isolated symbols and scattered statements from suspects begin to connect. The web tightens, and so does your sense of urgency. Just when you think you’re close to the truth, a seemingly ordinary character may reveal a hidden connection to the case from two decades ago, overturning everything you thought you knew.[/p][p]These twists aren’t forced; they gradually emerge from logic and details carefully laid out from the beginning of the story. When they finally fit into place, it’s like the web suddenly pulls taut around your neck, delivering a cinematic, breathless shock.[/p][p]Then comes the moment of choice: Will you expose the truth buried under the stars, no matter how painful, or protect the innocent by hiding part of it? Your decision shapes the ending—not in terms of good or evil, but as different weights tugging the threads of the story in multiple directions. Each ending offers a unique perspective on “truth and consequence,” leaving a lasting emotional impact.[/p][p]Like a film with an open ending, the story resolves but lingers in your mind, inviting reflection and the option to re-experience it from a new perspective.[/p][p] [/p][p][b]Characters: Where Emotion Takes Root[/b][/p][p]From the moment you enter the game, you step into the shoes of Gemini detective Lianshen. In a dusty archive room filled with old files, clues begin to fall into place, such as a slip in someone’s testimony or a hidden connection in a symbol. You’re drawn into Lianshen’s world and into his sharp, investigative mind.[/p][p]As the story progresses, his character comes into focus through your choices. His calm under pressure, his anxiety in moments of crisis… these layers shape both his growth and your emotional bond with him. When you stand at a crossroads, weighing friendship against duty, loyalty against law, those memories of shared struggles make the decision all the more personal.[/p][p]But it’s not just Lianshen. Every character in [i]The Zodiac Mystery[/i] is thoughtfully crafted. Their doubts and convictions, their wavering between reason and emotion, it all stems from unique personal histories and perspectives. Their choices affect your judgment, and your decisions shape their fates. This mutual influence creates tension and realism, leading to a deeper emotional connection that lasts long after the game ends.[/p]

notes.title: When Narrative Becomes the Soul of a Game
notes.notes: [p]In 2024, Black Myth: Wukong captured global attention with its striking narrative. It reimagines ancient mythology through epic storytelling, allowing players to feel the loneliness behind a hero’s rage.[/p][p]To the Moon unravels a story of love and regret through a slow, reverse chronology, peeling back time with each memory. Behind its quiet tone lies an emotional depth that lingers with many players.[/p][p]Heavy Rain experiments with multi-perspective branching narratives. As players control several characters in pursuit of the “Origami Killer,” every choice becomes a ripple in the story, each one reshaping the plot as the narrative explores the fringes of morality.[/p][p]The Rusty Lake series constructs an eerie universe by tying together 200 years of surreal family history. Its puzzle-box structure, loaded with religious symbols and reincarnation motifs, makes every playthrough feel like a descent into a strange yet coherent mythos.[/p][p]And now, The Zodiac Mystery brings its own approach. We’ve created a web-like structure where timelines intersect through astrological symbols. A decades-old cold case and the reopened present-day investigation unfold side by side, and each decision the player makes becomes a cog in the machinations of fate.[/p][p]When storytelling becomes the soul of a game, the experience transcends entertainment. What narrative has kept you awake at night? What line of dialogue still echoes in your mind? [/p][p]The answers may lie hidden in these unforgettable narrative masterpieces.[/p][p]#NarrativeGames #VisualNovel #ToTheMoon #HeavyRain #RustyLake #TheZodiacMystery[/p]

notes.title: No Walkthrough, No Script — In The Zodiac Mystery, You Live the Ending
notes.notes: [p]In real life, you’re always being pushed along by something, so you turn to games for a breath of fresh air, hoping to finally call the shots for once. But more often than not, that freedom turns out to be an illusion. “Choose A to gain 5 affection points.” “Select B to unlock a new map.” Even the trigger phrases for secret endings get dissected in walkthroughs until there’s nothing left to discover. Those so-called “multiple ending” games that promise butterfly-effect storylines often give you an experience where the developer is still pulling the strings.[/p][p]You think you’re the butterfly flapping your wings. But the direction, the motion, even the beat of your wings—all of it was written in code long before you hit "Start." Real immersion begins the moment you forget that a game is feeding you choices.[/p][p]It’s like wandering into a quiet alley late at night. You grip your phone flashlight and keep walking, heart pounding. Will there be a lamppost around the next corner, its glow falling softly on a wildflower blooming by the wall? Or maybe the half-closed wooden door creaks open just enough to let out a few curious meows, luring you to push it open and peek inside?[/p][p]That feeling of subtle anticipation mixed with complete unpredictability is the kind of immersion that makes you forget whether left or right leads to a hidden plot branch. You’re too busy thinking, “[i]Is that a note jammed into the crack in the wall[/i]?” that you stop caring whether you should’ve talked to that NPC earlier. Instead, you’re muttering to yourself, [i]“That guy’s acting weird... I should keep an eye on him.”[/i][/p][p][i]The Zodiac Mystery[/i] offers a sense of wandering through the unknown. The story flows like a living current, and as you float on its surface, even your smallest movements, where your eyes linger, how long your footsteps pause, might ripple outward into entirely different timelines, each carrying its own version of the truth.[/p][p]Maybe you’re investigating a crime scene and decide to open a bedroom wardrobe as you’re following a hunch. But in another timeline, you open the same wardrobe and find something completely different. It’s not that you missed a clue before, but that the contents were never fixed to begin with. Just like spinning a gacha machine, what drops out can be wildly different each time.[/p][p]A single difference like that can spark a whole new timeline. Maybe you find a rusty key smeared with blood, which leads you to a chest and the discovery of a murder driven by greed. The next time, you find a keepsake tangled with a bracelet, leading you down a path of emotional betrayal and long-buried resentment.[/p][p]It’s like holding a set of different game cartridges in your hand. Depending on what you plug in, the world that loads could be entirely different. With the bloodstained key, you’re playing “Treasure Hunt Gone Wrong.” With the bracelet, you’re dropped into “A Web of Lies and Love.” These aren’t branches of the same storyline; they’re entirely different mysteries, each with its own core. That thrilling shift, where finding a different item feels like entering a whole new game, is what will keep you coming back, again and again, wondering what story you’ll stumble into next.[/p][p]This is where [i]The Zodiac Mystery[/i] truly shines: it brings “choice” to the forefront of its story. It’s not a mechanism for reaching a prewritten ending, but a door to infinite possibilities. Every random encounter, every curious instinct, becomes a seed that grows into your own unique ending. When the game opens the door to a parallel timeline, it doesn’t tell you what to do. You discover the world at your own pace, guided by your own instincts, until you find your version of the truth.[/p][p]When the truth of “The Treasure Hunt Gone Wrong” is laid bare before you, maybe you’ll track the killer by following the relic’s path, or dig deeper into the family feud behind its origin. In “A Web of Lies and Love,” maybe you’ll focus on the betrayer’s state of mind, or unravel the hidden motivations of a key character tangled in that relationship.[/p][p]There are no right or wrong answers here. The truth is just a mirror, reflecting your inner leanings. You can follow where it leads or ignore it and follow your own instincts. Similar to a character build in an RPG, you can put all your points into brute strength, or master spells instead. It’s all about what you value most.[/p][p]And in the end, the conclusion you experience is the result of all the choices you made and the truths you decided to believe. In one version of “The Treasure Hunt Gone Wrong,” revealing the relic’s secret could spark a brutal clash over its ownership. Keep quiet, and maybe the killer will come forward, remorseful, bringing the case to a peaceful close. In “A Web of Lies and Love,” unmasking the betrayer might lead to a public showdown. But burying the truth could leave everyone safe, if not exactly whole.[/p][p]These endings may overlap between playthroughs or be completely different every time. Each one is shaped by the way you weigh your options. That reflection of human nature, embedded in the game’s final moments, is what gives each run its own distinct spark and leaves you walking away with something unexpected and unforgettable.[/p][p]That’s what games should be. Free from mechanical limits and rigid design. No one should dictate your path, and no system should overrule your choices. Like a tree growing freely in the wild, you can stretch toward the sun or spread your leaves in the shade. Each way of growing is unique. Each ending, shaped by your own hands, is irreplaceable. And that, at its core, is what makes a game truly enjoyable.[/p]

notes.title: A Narrative Journey Through Republican-Era Tianjin
notes.notes: [p]It all begins in Tianjin in the year 1935. An old diary found on a police desk opens a cold case, unearthing the lives of those trapped by fate. Once you touch that cover, the wheels of fate begin to turn.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/f79755ef815ff6e7d5e40cf21cc587e3d6ef7553.jpg"][/img] [/p][p][b]The Zodiac Mystery[/b] isn’t just a period crime story. It is a layered narrative, carefully crafted with the depth of a long-form drama and the tension of a complex mystery. Every choice the player makes pushes the story in a new direction, gradually reshaping the outcome.[/p][p][b]Stories That Begin at Home[/b][/p][p]The game’s emotional core is inspired by its creator’s own family history. Their stories of hardship, fractured bonds, and the struggle to love and be loved are all deeply woven into the game. Rather than focus on legends or heroes, [i]The Zodiac Mystery[/i] turns its gaze toward the raw, complicated ties within a family.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/e9dfa5c0bfbcf1a44d667a42a5804678ec0c5a1d.jpg"][/img] [/p][p]For years, our team researched real accounts from the Republican era, drawing from the struggles of everyday people to create a cast that feels grounded and alive. The characters' fears, their loyalty, and the mistakes they carry all mirror those once lived by a generation surviving in uncertain times.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/5758d6e2483333945ba56bee59b5f1999e18b06e.jpg"][/img] [/p][p]When a story grows from lived experiences and encapsulates the heart of human nature, it is able to transcend time. The wounds of our characters may reflect our own, but the hope they carry forward is the same light that helps all of us face the dark.[/p][p][b]One Core Mystery, Multiple Endings[/b][/p][p]At its heart, [i]The Zodiac Mystery[/i] is built around solving a string of astrological murders. Every mechanic, puzzle, and interaction is built to support that central goal. Investigating crime scenes, scouring case files, decrypting coded messages, and interrogating suspects all bring you closer to the truth.[/p][p]From the moment you open the diary detailing live sacrifices and demonic summoning rituals, the case takes hold of you. Sift through the archives, examine bloodstained scenes, and match each crime to the signs written in the stars. Each discovery, each question, and each silent stare from a suspect brings you one step closer.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/3c11d6a7dbf6f2d32cfcb115af7cc4a535a41bb7.jpg"][/img] [/p][p]Even so, no single answer is final, as your choices completely shift the outcome at key moments. You might offer a suspect redemption; or perhaps you might choose to pursue harsh justice. Your interpretations of astrological signs and subtle cues may even unlock hidden endings.[/p][p]The result is a story that remains focused, yet allows for replayability. Each new path reveals a different facet of the same enigma.[/p][p][b]The Cast Behind the Puzzle[/b][/p][p]The characters in [i]The Zodiac Mystery[/i] are complex, human, and deeply flawed. Take Lianshen, our protagonist. He isn’t a perfect detective; his childhood was marked by abandonment, violence, and loneliness. Learning became his escape, and a kind neighbor’s care helped him believe he could be more than the scars he carried.[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/1e096d076968e507936222da34e4fe8f47742531.jpg"][/img][/p][p]On the surface, he is talkative and optimistic, full of energy and confidence. But beneath that exterior lies someone shaped by insecurity. His dream of becoming a renowned detective is rooted in self-worth, revenge, and the desire to pay tribute to the person who once saved him.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/a4c9f0211c15ac333bc304d4bd32dc95085f1c2c.jpg"][/img] [/p][p]Lianshen’s every decision reflects the shadows and light of his past. Each choice the player makes carries weight precisely because this isn’t merely about solving a mystery—it’s about shaping a man who is still learning how to live with himself.[/p][p] [/p][p]In [i]The Zodiac Mystery[/i], the anchor is truth, but the ocean is human nature. What is justice? Who deserves redemption? What do we owe our past?[/p][p]By the end of your journey, you may find more than just a conclusion. You may find, in someone else’s story, a glimpse of your own, as well as a little courage to keep going.[/p]

notes.title: Some of the most unforgettable stories are those rooted in family.
notes.notes:
[p]Some of the most unforgettable stories are those rooted in family.

Maybe it’s the quiet ache of The Farewell, the chaos of Everything Everywhere All At Once, or the tender complexity in shows like This Is Us. Whether it's about love, loss, generational trauma, or the things left unsaid, stories about family often hit the hardest.

In The Zodiac Mystery, every character carries the weight of where they came from. Some are trying to escape it, while others are forced to confront it.

What’s a movie, show, book, or game that really captured the complexities of family for you?

Drop your favorites in the comments—we’d love to add them to our list!

[/p]

notes.title: The Zodiac Mystery: Portraits of Strength Shaped by Family
notes.notes:
[p][/p][p]In [i]The Zodiac Mystery[/i], each character’s story reflects the invisible weight of their family. The hardships they endured, the roots that wrapped around them tightly, and the innocence washed away by life’s storms did not cause them to wither. Rather, these struggles became the soil for something more resilient. They grew in the shadows, sprouted within cages, and turned every scar into nourishment, forging lives shaped by defiance, not surrender.[/p][p]The family we’re born into may be the ground we first break through, but it should never be what dictates when or how we bloom.[/p][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/ec58a48e60aa880e1ec1fd306a95e6848c2351eb.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]#FamilyIsNotTheFinalChapter[/b]
[b]Xiaowen: A Sunflower Growing Toward the Light[/b]
 She would tiptoe while serving tea as a child, afraid she might disturb someone. But she realized that facing her own shadow was what she truly feared. The motherly love she longed for was deliberately withheld; it was a dull knife that never cut clean. However, it taught her resilience. “They say I live in the shadows,” she says, “but the darker the shadow, the clearer the light.”[/p][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/886b2cd55ea9ca834636c96786b232bd25d86764.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]#AGoldenCageStillTrapsTheSoul[/b]
[b]Suxin: The Bird Who Created Her Own Path[/b]
 Raised as the perfect product of her mother’s upper-class reinvention, her skirts were always pressed, her smile always polite. But this soon became a prison. When she shattered her perfect image with a scream, she had already turned her mother’s expectations into a blade, forcefully cutting open a new path for herself.[/p][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/60ae9a8513abf5f7848c7783c74728232c29a510.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]#ScarsAreProofOfSurvival[/b]
[b]Jinrong: The Woman Who Rebuilt Herself from Ruins[/b]
 In her early years, she forged her shame into stepping stones. Later in life, she walled herself in with obsession and fear. Her coldness toward Xiaowen is a scar from cutting off part of herself, while her control over Suxin is the armor she wears to avoid falling again. She may have chosen the wrong tools, but she never stopped reconstructing her life from the rubble.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/db5b764b3c194beb2c65895b0a2f399f65b29a54.jpg"][/img] [/p][p][b]#RewriteYourOwnFate[/b]
[b]Lianshen: The Stargazer Who Turned Scars Into Light[/b]
 He was called “the unwanted child” growing up, until he realized he had to become his own home. His bruises were hidden away, and he studied until the pages curled—not just for knowledge, but to fight the feeling of being thrown away. A classmate once said to him, “If you work hard enough, you can change your fate,” and it became the tenant he lived by.[/p][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/a8413ae86d76fcd9f3f3ebe828f5f606d59307de.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]#TheWatcherSeesMore[/b]
[b]Chief Jiao: The Silent Watcher Behind the Curtain[/b]
 His father’s dominance felt like invisible chains, his mother’s illness a storm cloud that never broke. He saw strength softened by tenderness, and iron resolve eroded by despair. Eventually, his youthful idealism gave way to a hardened shell. Living between good and evil, he learned early on that the way out isn’t waiting to be rescued, it’s seeing yourself clearly.[/p][p] [/p][p]True strength is not the absence of weakness, but the ability to transform it into armor.
True growth isn’t cutting ties with the past, but choosing to carry those wounds, chains, and ruins forward, all while walking your own path.[/p][p]The stars will shift, fate will turn, and the only thing that can anchor your story
is the version of you who refuses to stop moving forward, no matter how bumpy the road.[/p]

notes.title: How Family Shapes Fate in The Zodiac Mystery
notes.notes: [p]In storytelling, as in life, everything begins with family. It is the source of every character’s choices, emotions, and fate. And in The Zodiac Mystery, we explore the quiet, hidden fractures that shape every character from the inside out.[/p][p]The game’s narrative is built on a simple belief: meaningful stories are rooted in family. It is home to humanity’s oldest emotions—love and resentment, dependence and rebellion, inheritance and defiance.[/p][p]In The Zodiac Mystery, those same tensions play out in the strained relationship between Jinrong and her daughters, Xiaowen and Suxin.[/p][p]Xiaowen, born when Jinrong worked as a dancer, carries the weight of her mother’s shame. Now climbing the social ladder, Jin Rong avoids Xiaowen like a living reminder of her past. Her emotional rejection is cold and deliberate as Xiaowen grows up starved of affection, tiptoeing around her mother, speaking softly, trying to earn love that never comes.[/p][p]Suxin, on the other hand, is Jin Rong’s “perfect daughter.” She acts as a symbol of her respectable, upper-class life. Suxin gets everything Xiaowen never did: care, attention, and privilege. But even this love has strings attached—Jinrong projects her ambition onto Suxin, demanding perfection and obedience, molding her into a vessel of social status. She lives in a gilded cage, beautiful yet suffocating.[/p][p]Every character in The Zodiac Mystery carries the weight of a family they didn’t choose. Their behaviors, beliefs, and emotional defenses all stem from the households that shaped them. From body language to branching choices, every detail has been carefully designed to reflect this theme.[/p][p]As a player, in addition to solving a crime, you are unlocking buried truths and emotional knots that run deeper than any mystery. The real pain is the quiet, painful patterns that families pass down through generations.[/p][p]And sometimes, breaking the curse means not rewriting the stars, but confronting the stories we’ve been told to keep hidden.[/p]

notes.title: Could your story find a home in “The Zodiac Mystery”?
notes.notes: [p]Every family has its scars; a "this is for your own good" that cut deep, an apology you needed but never received.[/p][p]We’re looking for stories that are personal yet familiar—moments that shaped who you are, or experiences you’ve witnessed that deserve to be heard.[/p][p]Some of them may find their way into the "The Zodiac Mystery," woven into characters so others can feel seen too.[/p][p]💬 Use the hashtag #MyStoryTZM to share a memory or experience, and your voice might help shape a character that someone else can resonate with.[/p][p]Because sometimes it’s not the stars that guide us, but the courage to face our wounds.[/p]

notes.title: "The Zodiac Mystery": The stars reveal your path, but family shapes your scars.
notes.notes: [p][b]Stories about the complexities of familial trauma have been a staple in the entertainment industry for a reason. The pain they depict is real, impactful, and most of all, universal.[/b][/p][p]In "The Bear," Carmy inherits his late brother’s restaurant as he is still grappling with his suicide. This tragedy, coupled with complicated intergenerational struggles, burdens the family he was born into; all the while, he builds a found family that provides him with newfound support.[/p][p][/p][p] At the heart of "Everything Everywhere All at Once" are powerful themes of generational trauma and the emotional distance that can grow between immigrant parents and their children. Through Evelyn and her daughter Joy’s journey, we witness a story about reconnecting with those we love.[/p][p][/p][p]13‑year‑old Jamie is arrested for murdering a female classmate in the 2025 miniseries Adolescence. The show dives into how his family grapples with the aftermath, revealing the devastating ripple effects of trauma on parents, siblings, and even the community.[/p][p][/p][p]As for "The Zodiac Mystery," the struggles each character faces aren’t just written in the stars—they are carved into their hearts like scars.[/p][p][/p][p]Like Orion chasing Sirius across the sky, every character is caught in the orbit of their past, unknowingly retracing the shadows cast by their families. Some grow thorns, some feign joy, some build walls, and others disappear completely. [/p][p]Regardless of how our characters cope with their trauma, it all traces back to one thing: family.[/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Zodiac Confessions—Let’s talk about your favorite star sign!
notes.notes: [p]✨ I’ll start! As someone who spends every day buried in drafts, I’ve unofficially crowned myself a “Writing Gemini.” I’m constantly juggling ideas—breaking down topics on one side, typing away at lightning speed on the other. I can write heartfelt personal essays, then switch seamlessly to technical articles. It’s like my brain is split in two, and it even amazes me sometimes![/p][p]⚡ I’ve got a soft spot for Aquarius. Their bold “I make my own rules” energy is so inspiring. To me, freedom isn’t about running away; it’s about turning everyday life into art.[/p][p]🤣 On the other hand, collaborating with a Virgo can be a little nerve-wracking. I once had a colleague who edited a proposal using color-coded highlights just to mark the spacing between punctuation marks. They flagged things like the difference between “who” and “whom” and rewrote entire paragraphs for clarity. Then they sent back 37 revision notes with the comment, “This is just the first draft.”[/p][p]🔍 Now it’s your turn![/p][p]✅ What’s your favorite zodiac sign?[/p][p]✅ Is there one that you instantly click with, or one you’d rather steer clear of?[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/85456db90db2b4fdf569f9e82c06a46f3f25f62c.jpg"][/img][/p]

notes.title: The Cast of "The Zodiac Mystery": How the Twelve Signs Shape Their Fate
notes.notes: [h2]A storm brews over Tianjin as the stars align.[/h2][p] [/p][p]When the hazy fog of Tianjin's Liulitai district meets the twelve zodiac signs, a mystery unfolds—a puzzle in which astrology becomes the key to unlocking human nature. From detectives to artists, dancers to everyday citizens, everyone in "The Zodiac Mystery" carries the mark of their zodiac sign.[/p][p] [/p][p][b]Gemini: Lianshen, Suxin, Wenqiang[/b][/p][p]This sign is born with the unique ability to completely immerse themselves in perception and observation. Gemini aims to uncover truth in the world, see everything they possibly can, and understand new ways of doing things. They are often great helpers with sharp minds. Their keen eyes and nimble hands often allow them to handle things skillfully.[/p][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/1bd9a29185f8b2006b9ae65d126cc89726e37ebd.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]Scorpio: Chief Jiao, Xiaohong[/b][/p][p]This sign constantly lives every moment like it's their last, leaving behind no regrets. This strong sense of crisis is both a blessing and a curse. Scorpio can deftly handle all kinds of uncertainties, but their weakness lies in obsessing over the immutable past and worrying about the future that has yet to come. This sign is also known as the quintessential romantic, as they will do anything for love.[/p][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/70decb68c52c59e9ebab37d551320bccd4e9ed72.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]Aquarius: Tianbao, Xiaowen, Tianzhong[/b][/p][p]The beginning and end of this sign's life is marked by freedom. For Aquarius, doing whatever they like without pressure or influence from outside factors is the ideal way of life. Aquarius can be difficult to understand, though they are typically smart and discerning. This sign is able to see both fine details and the bigger picture. This intelligence helps Aquarius consistently view things from their own special perspective.[/p][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/931699dd38ae164321768474505532cd67584eb9.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]Leo: Jinrong, Hongyan[/b][/p][p]More than any other sign, Leo is aware of their mortality at any given moment—yesterday is gone, and tomorrow may never come. They want to seize the moment while they still can, finding hope within it. Leo doesn't like keeping secrets and always reveals them sooner or later, feeling relieved when they can finally get it off their chest. Performing freely onstage like a child is always a highlight for a Leo.[/p][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/a0bcc992c0a48d655fd7d273d5a9286d8933a3e1.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]Libra: Xiaoping[/b][/p][p]This sign loves all things beautiful and has a great eye for aesthetics. Libra is often willing to sacrifice or suppress their own feelings to maintain superficial peace. They are elegant communicators. When Libra is up against a strong personality or in a disadvantageous situation, they will unwittingly stay silent, sometimes acting distracted or hesitant. However, this is only out of self-preservation.[/p][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/13e4d7c4ef2419b2f19a418fb0cb73bef4910065.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]Capricorn: Xiaorong[/b][/p][p]Capricorn is a climber. This sign hopes to make the world shine brighter with their dreams and abilities. For Capricorn, understanding how to make themselves happy is perhaps their most difficult conundrum. They often wonder where life is leading them. It is not accolades or applause, but self-acceptance and independence. Both must be achieved, as gaining inner recognition is the only answer for this sign.[/p][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/cb92fb69c4f7eea700094675f06a5bab6ccca5f3.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]Virgo: Xiaojuan[/b][/p][p]This sign's truest form lies in being meticulously observant, harboring an extreme desire for growth, and finding fun in monotony. They are always ready to help and serve others, seeing it as a form of self-discovery. More than anything, assisting others acts as a conduit for Virgo to express themselves and realize their pursuit of perfection by providing help and support.[/p][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/16b4e5df1f6476e5075f5c23dc2f2eb3431b872a.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]Pisces: Zhuzi[/b][/p][p]This sign's mind is a microcosm of the universe, acting as both their primary resource and refuge. Pisces has an incredible imagination that can be a double-edged sword. Their sense of boundaries can often be an issue, but it is also an important key to managing any and all of their relationships.[/p][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/34bba6b46592bc63e2d61b096564014f582e36b3.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]Taurus: Hongmei[/b][/p][p]This sign experiences the world through their senses, particularly tactile contact. They are unable to confront the existence of the world through their mind alone. A sense of security can be both their biggest opportunity and challenge. If Taurus can bravely let down their guard and avoid being too stubborn, the world will come alive in their hands.[/p][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/4ab478a80ff262a699054605ac155bc3d58b0f20.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]Sagittarius: Meixia, Yan[/b][/p][p]For this sign, life is an adventure. With that in mind, they eschew all sense of security, living independently and freely as they experience the world. A love for freedom and pursuing the meaning of life is Sagittarius's main purpose. This sign believes there is no point in holding on to or living in the past because the future is already here.[/p][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/d3b56185eb27ec312a65e2c0ae9d0cc693e214ca.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]Aries: Jianwei, Meina[/b][/p][p]Defined by fierce vitality and courage, this sign often represents the ability to overcome any threats, obstacles, or doubt through sheer willpower. They behave boldly, communicate directly, and love passionately. Of all the signs, Aries is least likely to hold back when expressing themselves. Once Aries zeroes in on a goal, they will move forward without hesitation, persisting until it is achieved.[/p][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/6455c9ef6fabab9b73ac1524f93e0a7eff361a6c.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]Cancer: Xiaoli[/b][/p][p]For this sign, the world is structured around emotion. They are motivated by a strong sense of subjectivity. Cancer aims to experience consciousness, feeling every nuance of life. Though they can see hellish discord in life, Cancer opposes all disparities, violating common sense to love, trust, and accept all of the emotions that come with existing.[/p][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/4e7c9c36524fa678570833bf4068197afbb5644a.jpg"][/img][/p][p]The zodiac characteristics are not only personality traits—they also act as hidden clues that push the plot forward.[/p][p] [/p][p]Pulled between personal choices and their cosmic fate, the characters sketch a strange yet vivid star map representing humanity.[/p][p] [/p][p]A tangled astrological mystery awaits! Are you ready to dive in?[/p][p] [/p]

notes.title: An Astrological Prison: The Metaphors of "The Zodiac Mystery"
notes.notes: [p]After a male corpse is discovered in his own blood-soaked art studio, the gears of fate begin to turn, locking a group of individuals in a prison shaped by the stars. "The Zodiac Mystery" utilizes a dual narrative structure to peel back the layers of love, betrayal, and tangled pasts.[/p][p] [/p][p]Each character becomes a pawn on destiny's chessboard, powerless against forces beyond their control. Marked by the zodiac, they are trapped in a cycle of desire and fear, transforming into the very things they dread most.[/p][p] [/p][p][b]Under the Stars: Metaphors of Darkness, Silence, and Death[/b][/p][p]"Only in silence the word, Only in dark the light, Only in dying life." Amidst this labyrinth of signs and symbols, the core mechanics of "The Zodiac Mystery" draw inspiration from Ursula K. Guin's insight.[/p][p] [/p][p]In astrology, a planet "in fall" represents struggle and challenge—just like the darkest moments before cracking a case. But if you can break through those difficulties, the path to truth becomes clear.[/p][p] [/p][p]Silence, on the other hand, is like the neglected details of a case, concealing key clues; exploring these nooks and crannies may reveal crucial information.[/p][p] [/p][p]As for death, it may close one door, but it opens another. A dead end in the investigation may point toward fresh leads, allowing players to piece together the living truth from what once seemed lost.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/3b0b0cb0fd9ed44c83cf13d61eeae9ca31691675.jpg"][/img][/p][p] [b]A Game in the Shadows: Who Holds the Killer's Chart?[/b][/p][p]In "The Zodiac Mystery," the web of characters is as complex as the crim itself. Lianshen, a police officer and amateur astrologer who just returned from overseas, begins his search for the truth. By his side is Chief Jiao, a seasoned detective, mentor, and friend—though he seemingly has some secrets of his own.[/p][p] [/p][p]Jinrong, a suspect related to the case, is the headmistress of the dance school. Once the pride of her family, she became a lowly dance hostess and clawed her way back to power with ruthless ambition. Her daughter, Xiaowen, grew up surrounded by hardship, but she quietly yearns for freedom. Other students at the dance school, such as Xiaohong or Xiaoping, each have their own distinct desires and backstories.[/p][p]In this astrological case, is Jinrong the one who would stop at nothing for her own gain? Or did Xiaowen strike due to secrets hidden in her past? Or maybe someone else lurks in the shadows, using astrology to conceal their crime?[/p][p] [/p][p]Anyone could be the murderer. Their fates are all tightly intertwined, woven together in a web of mystery.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/e2f29c4be2d127c6e41813a02ea4ce6071e371dc.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]The Logic in Investigating: Finding the Truth Through Examination and Interrogation[/b][/p][p]As the investigation unfolds, players must examine the crime scene closely, systematically sorting through clues to build a foundation of evidence. Then, based on their findings, they must sift through complex archives to separate truth from falsehood and back up reasonable interrogations with suspects.[/p][p] [/p][p]When a suspect's testimony contradicts physical evidence or archives, when they become evasive at critical moments, players must press onward, digging deeper to expose the flaws in their lies.[/p][p] [/p][p]This cycle of investigation and interrogation requires players to carefully trace connections between clues, using cause-and-effect logic to gradually unravel the intricate web of deception spun throughout the stars.[/p][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/f9ba402f98819c62496246cbab030ad8625e8f4c.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/95b99008a88e7d64bd74a54529ad33287f62734c.png"][/img][/p][p]When you uncover the spark of a breakthrough buried deep in the dusty archives,[/p][p]when you hear echoes of a decades-old crime in a shadowy art studio,[/p][p]when you decode a star chart at the core of a mysterious sacrificial ritual...[/p][p]you will realize: every paradox is a metaphor shaped by fate.[/p][p]Breaking through them is the rite of passage that transforms you from a pawn in the game... into the one who moves the pieces.[/p]

notes.title: "The Zodiac Mystery": A Battle Between Truth and Destiny
notes.notes: [p]When zodiac characteristics collide with a string of mysterious crimes, every word uttered by each character carries hidden weight.[/p][p][/p][p]Lianshen's doubts, Chief Jiao's philosophy, Jinrong's ruthless resolve... they are all tangled in a web of suspense.[/p][p][/p][p]In a maze riddled with unknowns, how will each pen their own story? Can the truth pierce the fog and finally come to light?[/p][p][/p][p]Follow along as we uncover more surprises behind "The Zodiac Mystery"![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/8f5ea11609e048b785eb6d4f558f8340e4b967c6.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/e26fd0544ed1311ef91c8cd2c0c6030ab92a1a07.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/9927f1bc8923c92d13a28c7e8d229c9f267de911.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/6521b759e2c04c4040d474e9702f6bd13276e20b.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/4a11e0d341f94fe6ac90d57f38ea4631fdbf4100.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/fdbd44da0f011af7ea4746bcf667d6758a6c9433.jpg"][/img][/p]

notes.title: The Cast of "The Zodiac Mystery": The Twelve Signs, Trapped
notes.notes: [p]In "The Zodiac Mystery," every character, whether it be truth-seeking detectives or suspects wrapped up in a web of lies, is caught in the complex storm of human nature. The twelve zodiac signs act like invisible threads, tightly binding the destinies of those residing in the Liulitai area of Tianjin. These souls, marked by the stars, are drawn into fate's harrowing game; it is a journey marked by life, death, and redemption on the hazy road to the truth.[/p][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/cca08092326ff555b883215b22ab3d5e562f0e22.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]The "Mind Probe": Lianshen (Gemini)[/b][/p][p]Role: Player character — a young police officer in Liulitai, Tianjin[/p][p]"What is the truth?" "What secrets lie beneath the facade?" Lianshen's quiet thoughts constantly burn like an eternal flame. Gemini's sharp wit and adaptability allow him to navigate complex environments with ease. However, he must tread carefully when overwhelmed with a flood of conflicting clues, or he may lose his way at any moment.[/p][p] [/p][p][b]Abyssal Observer: Chief Jiao (Scorpio)[/b][/p][p]Role: Seasoned officer and archives manager[/p][p]Faced with an impossibly complicated case, Chief Jiao's gaze doesn't fall on the evidence, but rather into the abyss. "What lies at the edge of life and death?" Scorpio's discernment grants him penetrating insight amidst deception. In a silent standoff with death, he guards the key to the ultimate truth.[/p][p] [/p][p][b]Defier of Fate: Jinrong (Leo)[/b][/p][p]Role: Dance school headmistress[/p][p]From celebrated debutant to lowly dance hostess, Jinrong swallowed her shame and humiliation, navigating neon shadows to hunt down her own "prey." Finally, she clawed her way to the position of headmistress. Every scar screams out the same truth: "I make my own fate—whoever stands in my way will die!"[/p][p] [/p][p][b]Seeker of Freedom: Xiaowen (Aquarius)[/b][/p][p]Role: Jinrong's daughter[/p][p]Xiaowen's birth began with tragedy when Jinrong was sold to a dance hall, and her childhood was defined by poverty and separation. Even so, her father's love brought her a sense of warmth—until he died under mysterious circumstances. Upon moving to Tianbao's property with her mother, her innocence was further shattered. Over and over, she asks herself, "Will I ever find freedom in this life?"[/p][p] [/p][p][b]A Light in the Dark: Xiaohong (Scorpio)[/b][/p][p]Role: Dance school student[/p][p]The abyss has claimed countless souls, but it can't take the light inside Xiaohong. "Stay optimistic. Be strong. Rewrite your destiny!" This stubborn spark, refusing to be snuffed out, becomes her guide through the darkness. She becomes a symbol of hope for others, something to reach out and touch in their darkest moments.[/p][p] [/p][p][b]Balancer of Fate: Xiaoping (Libra)[/b][/p][p]Role: Dance school student[/p][p]"I never know what choice to make... What should I do?" Libra's instinct for balance becomes Xiaoping's biggest burden. Her constant hesitation and attempts to please everyone around her slowly morph into a blade—one that cuts through her opportunities, dreams, and ultimately, her future.[/p][p] [/p][p][b]The stars shift. A murder unfolds.[/b][/p][p]Can you look past the constellations and uncover the brutal truth beyond the stars?[/p][p]Light and darkness, good and evil; two sides of the same coin, the boundary long blurred by fate.[/p][p]Only one thing is certain:[b] the end of this star map holds no guaranteed answers[/b]...[/p][p]because the path to rewrite destiny is in YOUR hands—as long as YOU have the courage to find the truth and face your choices head-on.[/p]

notes.title: Creator's Notes: Memories Fade, But Human Nature Endures
notes.notes: [p]Today, We'd like to talk about what lies at the core of "[i]The Zodiac Mystery[/i]." Our goal was to combine the allure of astrology, everyday life in Republican-era Tianjin, and the head-scratching suspense of puzzles into a unique mystery adventure.[/p][p]A decades-old cold case, long resolved for over twenty years, is finally revived by a mysterious diary. This premise was born from our obsession with time and memory, leading to a fascinating question—can truths buried by the flow of time ever really stay hidden?[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/2eb0694e726c3c8d36cfefcf0127c3a21350c8c8.png"][/img][/p][p]An officer returning from abroad with a penchant for astrology gets unexpectedly drawn into the case, mirroring the player's own confusion and curiosity when starting the game. Within the narrative, astrological elements can serve as both clues and shackles; we believe every individual's behavior and choices carry unique "astrological markers." Aries's impulsiveness, Cancer's obsession, Leo's pride, Virgo's meticulousness, Libra's indecisiveness... These characteristics reshape as motives, transform into murder weapons, and turn the zodiac into something more than just mere entertainment—it becomes a vital cog in the deductive machine.[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/18b7ae823b2bfb0037ed558943121989f6eef221.png"][/img][/p][p]When designing the in-game environments, we immersed ourselves in the suspenseful atmosphere of everyday life in Republican-era Tianjin. From an eerie art studio to a beach house riddled with concealed dangers, every setting in the game has two sides. What appear as typical crime scenes for players to explore are actually riddled with astrological elements and references—but no spoilers for now! Uncover the truth for yourself when you play.[/p][p]The proudest achievement is our groundbreaking multiple-ending feature. We refuse to pigeonhole players' choices as simply "right" or "wrong." Each ending is a possibility that could ostensibly play out in a parallel timeline. Perhaps you thought you had the culprit dead to rights—but a single, overlooked astrological symbol could clear their involvement. Impressive deductive skills may only be the tip of the iceberg. The sense of uncertainty is rooted in our deep respect for the complexity of human nature; there is no black and white, good or evil—only souls warped by desire and obsession.[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/c113340f2fdba8ea9eee82e1d9cb5b42b02b3812.png"][/img][/p][p]"[i]The Zodiac Mystery[/i]" isn't just a puzzle game. It's a mirror, reflecting our own obsession with the truth, fear of the unknown, and never-ending exploration of the light and darkness concealed within human nature. The moment you open that mysterious diary, you become a co-conspirator in this story.[/p][p]Are you ready? A decades-old astrological mystery awaits—and it's time for you to pen the conclusion.[/p]

notes.title: The Astrological Ensemble: A Republican-era Mystery with Zodiac Logic
notes.notes:
Republican-era Tianjin was a classic semi-feudal, semi-colonial city, housing concessions from nine foreign powers—Britain, France, the U.S., Germany, Italy, Russia, Japan, Austria-Hungary, and Belgium, each with its own embassies and consulates. Diplomats, envoys, and businessmen from around the globe converged there, essentially turning the city into its own “nation within a nation.”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/a850133493f6a08de6e4ce975a5764e56c87e9cc.png[/img]
Along the Haihe River, Gothic church spires stood in striking juxtaposition with the upturned eaves of Chinese roofs. Western brokers in tailored suits rubbed shoulders with merchants donning traditional robes. The rumble of trams mingled with the shouts of street vendors, interweaving Eastern and Western cultures to create a vivid tapestry.

Western culture spread rapidly within these concessions, as churches, schools, and hospitals established by Christian missions sprang up throughout the city. Meanwhile, mysticism, including tarot cards and astrological readings, also rode this wave to gain popularity. Back then, it wasn’t uncommon to see horoscope columns printed alongside Peking opera schedules in Tianjin newspapers, and astrological salons in concession clubs were as lively as the storytelling performances in teahouses. In Chinese neighborhoods, traditional practices like fortune-telling and Feng Shui still persisted. The collision of these two worlds led to new forms of divination—an “East-meets-West” style of astrological reading. This cultural melding didn’t just change how people lived; it reshaped the city itself, fostering the perfect environment for bizarre rumors and mysterious incidents to flourish.

That is precisely how [i]The Zodiac Mystery[/i] came to life, rooted in Tianjin’s local life and shaped by the strange allure of astrology.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/364612828a4d6a7af4e256af693bc7de538d9355.png[/img]

Our game’s lead producer is an experienced astrologer and a lifelong fan of detective fiction. She has poured years of astrological knowledge and a deep love for the mystery genre into the “The Zodiac Mystery.” The game centers on an ensemble cast, weaving a tightly-knit web of characters with unique personalities and distinct astrological traits. Every character’s behavior and fate are quietly guided by the zodiac to create a story as intricate as a star chart.

Take Aries, for example—their impulsive passion often leads them to be bold and direct, their motives igniting in a sudden burst of emotion. On the other hand, Cancer is deeply sensitive and driven by the need to protect what they cherish most. Each character’s behavior and motivations are led by the invisible strings of their sign, making their actions unique yet traceable. Players can use their own understanding of astrology to predict and analyze their behavior, unlocking a fascinating deductive adventure full of possibilities.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/1ba2492e7095347bc00b95ebef120278d8968e77.png[/img]

At the same time, we’ve also closely tied complex star charts and zodiac symbols to clues in the game, combining these elements with our branching narrative system. Every investigation, every deduction, and every choice a player makes could shatter their original theory, rewriting the path and conclusion of their story.

In fact, the incorporation of astrology into the mystery genre has been a long-held and popular tradition, becoming an enduring and important sub-classification. Soji Shimada’s “The Tokyo Zodiac Murders” is one such classic, utilizing astrology to expose the madness of human nature and the mystique of astrology in astonishing ways. Eleanor Catton’s “The Luminaries,” which earned the Booker Prize, wove alliances and betrayals into a twisting tale of secrets and lies, putting the struggles of human nature under pressure on full display. These works prove just how powerful and lasting this genre can be. “The Zodiac Mystery” is honored to draw inspiration from them, crafting a uniquely immersive puzzle for players to unravel.

We’re confident that this game, with complex deductions and a deeply immersive narrative, will give players an exhilarating thrill of revealing a mystery and uncovering truths that subvert everything they could have imagined.

Are you ready to find your truth in the fog of stars and human nature?

notes.title: Threads of the Zodiac: Obsession Weaving Through an Astrological Haze
notes.notes:
In "The Zodiac Mystery," obsession flows through the Republican-era setting like a silent yet raging undercurrent, pushing the investigation closer to an answer.

Lianshen is a quick-witted Gemini and a top graduate from the police academy. After studying abroad in Europe, he returns to China with a burning passion for justice. Though he could have chosen an easier or even more promising career, he decides to work at the Liulitai Police Station in Tianjin, pursuing truth on the front lines. After getting sucked into a difficult case and realizing a longtime friend may be involved, Lianshen remains steadfast in his pursuit, even though the choice between loyalty and justice nearly tears him apart. His obsession acts as a guide, helping him tune out all background noise. With all the sharp instincts of a typical Gemini, he pieces together clues as if he is spinning a web, grabbing hold of every thread and leaving nowhere for the truth to hide.

Chief Jiao, a Scorpio and seasoned detective, harbors a quiet yet unwavering obsession with justice, buried under decades of experience. Though he was once the pride of the police academy, he has long since pushed those accolades aside. When faced with a painful choice between love and justice, he hesitates. However, his steadfast obsession with doing what's right pushes him to stand firm. He uses Scorpio's signature calm and sharp insight to guide the investigation forward as he works alongside Lianshen. He is not only solving a case—he is passing on his legacy. Through Linashen, he hopes the torch of justice will continue to burn.

In addition to Lianshen and Chief Jiao, other key characters such as Tianbao, Jinrong, and Xiaowen are also driven by their obsessions. Some try to make up for past regrets, while others chase a future they can't stop dreaming about. These fixations clash and interweave like gears in a machine, pushing the tale forward through a tangled mass of love, hate, and hidden agendas.

In this strange and unpredictable mystery, obsession is both a flicker of light guiding toward the truth and an invisible vine constricting each soul. Every character is caught in their own struggle as players experience the heat, weight, and chaos of the path to justice.

"The Zodiac Mystery" showcases the depth and complexity of obsession through carefully layered storytelling, constructing a world full of realism and dramatic tension. Every hard-earned deduction, every challenging decision shines with the flame of obsession.

Dive into "The Zodiac Mystery" now...
Unravel the clues one thread at a time...
And experience a mystery driven by obsession, uncovering long-buried truths.

notes.title: The Zodiac Mystery: Human Nature Under the Weight of Conflict
notes.notes:
Lianshen: Twin Flames, Illuminating a Path Through the Mystery

In "The Zodiac Mystery," amidst the foggy backdrop of the Republican Era, the bond shared by Lianshen and Chief Jiao shines like twin flames piercing through the darkness. Lianshen, a quick-witted Gemini officer, approaches the case with a unique perspective. Due to his lonely childhood, he walks the path of truth alone—until Chief Jiao appears, like a beacon of light illuminating his world.

To Lainshen, Chief Jiao is the embodiment of wisdom. He admires Chief Jiao's calm disposition while unraveling complex cases, and is even more moved by his mentorship. Chief Jiao is more than a teacher who imparts Lianshen with investigative knowledge; he is also a cherished friend who fills the emotional void in his life. Each time Lianshen finds himself torn between loyalty and justice, Chief Jiao lifts the fog with his quiet strength and experience.

For Chief Jiao, his feelings for Lianshen run even deeper. He sees a reflection of himself in Lianshen, a young, sharp man who hasn't yet been worn down by reality or experienced failure. This is precisely why Chief Jiao is willing to give everything, burning himself like a flame to fuel Lianshen's pursuit of justice and assist him in achieving the dreams he himself never could. This pair, though separated by age, navigate numerous cases as both mentor and student, as well as friends. They use each other's light to illuminate the long road to the truth.



Chief Jiao: A Guardian Across Time, Forging Justice With Light

In the suspenseful world of "The Zodiac Mystery," Chief Jiao and Lianshen's connection is one of the most moving throughlines. As a Scorpio and veteran detective, Chief Jiao conceals his unfulfilled desire for justice behind a composed exterior. However, he sees the ideal version of himself within Lianshen—brave, unyielding, and free.



Chief Jiao acts as a silent guardian, utilizing his lifetime of experience as a guidepost for Lianshen's journey. When Lianshen struggles between concepts of friendship and justice, Chief Jiao patiently guides him to look inward. When his youthful impulsiveness runs rampant, Chief Jiao steps in to help him course-correct. For Chief Jiao, helping Lianshen realize his vision of justice is not only a way to mentor the next generation—it is also a form of personal redemption.

To Lianshen, Chief Jiao is like the sun. Lonely since childhood, he feels an unprecedented warmth and companionship in Chief Jiao. His wisdom, composure, and care fill the holes in Lianshen's heart. Together, these two unlikely partners make a formidable investigative team. One charges ahead as the other strategizes behind the scenes. Across the distance of generations, they rely on each other as kindred spirits. Their story, set against the backdrop of Republican-era China, is one of enduring friendship, justice, and ideals.


In this case riddled with puzzles, the bond that Chief Jiao and Lianshen share is tested and strengthened by trust and suspicion, understanding and conflict. Their struggles, interwoven with suspects' motives, emotional tension, and unseen forces, lie at the intricate heart of "The Zodiac Mystery." This very complexity makes their bond all the more profound and powerful as they walk together in pursuit of the truth.

notes.title: The Zodiac Mystery: Unraveling the Personas of Lianshen & Chief Jiao
notes.notes:
In The Zodiac Mystery, Lianshen and Cheif Jiao's distinct zodiac traits make them the key players in cracking the case.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/22f38037820c6b2abfbd02983b1e63966f31b46d.jpg[/img]
Lianshen, a Gemini, has an agile mind and is sharp as a tack. When examining a theft case with sparse clues, his quick intuition allows him to find contradictions in suspects’ subtle reactions and statements, and he cleverly connects seemingly irrelevant details to uncover the truth. His social skills and instinctive humor as a Gemini help him break barriers and extract key information from multiple angles.

As a Scorpio, Chief Jiao is as steady and mysterious as an iceberg. Faced with a crime scene, his intense focus allows him to pick apart every tiny clue like a treasure hunter—even footprints and scratches can help him deduce a criminal’s modus operandi. When the investigation hits a dead end, Chief Jiao’s decisiveness allows him to consider new insights and lead his team to the truth. Lianshen’s razor-sharp wit and Chief Jiao’s calm precision perfectly juxtapose each other, adding a certain charm to the story.

notes.title: The Zodiac Mystery: The Spark of Genius, the Power of Obsession
notes.notes:
Does genius truly exist? What does it look like?

Perhaps The Zodiac Mystery holds the answers to these questions. Those who use a deep understanding of astrology to discover clues within celestial patterns undoubtedly possess the traits of a genius. They catch details others might miss, seamlessly blending astrological knowledge with logical reasoning. For instance, some characters can predict suspects' actions based on astrological changes. This keen insight and unique mindset are the true embodiment of a genius. 
What’s more, obsession is often the core driving force behind breakthroughs in their cases. Take Lianshen as an example—his nearly religious pursuit of the truth constantly pushes him to persevere. Even when clues are scarce and the pressure is on, his obsession helps him continue exploring. His relentless drive ensures he never overlooks a potential lead, and he ultimately unravels the mystery.

In The Zodiac Mystery, genius and obsession intertwine, driving the story forward and allowing players to appreciate both the beauty and difficulty in deduction.

notes.title: The Zodiac Mystery: Celestial Intrigue in the Republican-Era
notes.notes:
Dear Detectives,

The Republican-era world depicted in The Zodiac Mystery is rife with mysterious cold cases, where astrology acts as an invisible hand, weaving intrigue and puzzles into each crime.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45417059/ecfc278cc99dbd70eb4708551e5b060b30b3187d.jpg[/img]
Our story is set during China’s turbulent Republican Era, when strange incidents were a dime a dozen. This particular case seems impossible to crack at first, and the astrological element only adds another layer of confusion. In the locked-room murder, for example, a strange astrological symbol left next to the deceased seemingly acts as a sign from the stars. According to astrology, different signs exhibit various energies under certain celestial conditions; in The Zodiac Mystery, these energies are closely linked to the development of the case and the character’s fates.

Various forces push and pull at the case—shadowy conspiracies, entangled emotions, and brilliant deductive reasoning. Just like real detectives during the Republican Era, our protagonists Lianshen and Chief Jiao use their wisdom and courage to traverse the fog of this mystery, untangling the complex connections between this case and astrology.

Step into The Zodiac Mystery to experience a unique journey, uncovering the link between this Republican-era mystery and astrology!
